evals.prompt: /tts-output Write a 3-minute calm, warm narration explaining how home solar panels and batteries work for a first-time buyer. Save it as solar-intro.md.
evals.expected_output: A ~450-word speech-ready .md script: paragraphs of about 20-60 words, no short headings, numbers spelled out, straight apostrophes, no caps/emphasis/tags, tone carried by wording; linter run and clean; report gives word count, minutes and suggested --speed/--pause/--voice.

evals.prompt: /tts-output Turn draft.md into something Kokoro can read out as an excited product-launch announcement.
evals.expected_output: A new file (draft left untouched) rewriting the draft: digits, %, $, Q3, e.g., URLs, table and bullet list converted to spoken prose; ALL CAPS and !!! removed; short punchy sentences grouped inside 30-50 word paragraphs; excited-mood flags suggested (speed ~1.05-1.1, pause ~0.3, Heart or Bella).

evals.prompt: /tts-output I need a short sad, reflective passage (about one minute) for the end of a documentary episode about a closed-down mining town. The voice should sound like it's asking the listener questions.
evals.expected_output: ~150-word script; explains that Kokoro cannot raise pitch on questions or act sad, so questions are made obvious by wording and sadness by plain words, pacing, paragraph breaks and slower speed (~0.85-0.9) with longer pauses (~0.7-1.0); no fake emotion tags.

evals.prompt: /tts-output Write a 5-minute morning devotion on good habits. Open with a Bible verse (Proverbs 6:10) and quote it in Afrikaans, then a list of things people put off, and end with a prayer.
evals.expected_output: A speech-ready .md script that avoids the structure traps: one opening sentence instead of stacked short headings; the list of put-off things folded into one 20-60 word paragraph instead of one line each; no bold-only lines; 'Father,' and 'Amen' folded into neighbouring paragraphs; the reference written as 'Proverbs chapter six, verse ten'; the whole script in English, with the Afrikaans verse translated into English and the original Afrikaans text nowhere in the file (Kokoro does not support Afrikaans; the report says so); no --- rules; linter run with no short-paragraph group listing more than a few lines.
